title: ai_adoption_in_large_company
primary_keyword: AI adoption in a large company
claim: AI fails in enterprise marketing because teams buy tools before defining the governance bottleneck.

evidence.detail: Observed across multiple enterprise marketing transformations where software licenses outpaced workflow definition by six months, resulting in zero net change to output velocity.

reel_script.voiceover: Buy the tool. Argue later. That is how enterprise software deployments start.
reel_script.direction: Direct cut to text on screen, measured pace.

items.label: Software procured
items.detail: Licenses secured with no process map

reel_script.onscreen: The software is fast. The review is dead.
reel_script.voiceover: The software produces assets in seconds. But the review queue still takes three weeks.
reel_script.direction: Pan slightly, maintaining neutral professional tone.

reel_script.voiceover: Speed was never the bottleneck in a governed organisation. Risk was.
If you lead AI adoption in a large company, stop buying licenses and run this three-step check.
reel_script.direction: Shift visual cue to framework checklist.

reel_script.voiceover: First, map every legal review gate. If it takes ten days, faster generation creates a backlog.
reel_script.direction: Focus on the first checklist item.

reel_script.voiceover: AI does not fix a broken approval chain. It just makes the queue twice as long.
Software without governance is just expensive noise.
reel_script.direction: Final title card with named principle.

caption:
Buy the tool. Argue later.

AI adoption in a large company stalls not because the models are weak, but because teams treat a governance problem as a procurement problem.

When you introduce generative tools without fixing the review gate, you do not increase output. You just increase the size of the digital dustbin waiting for legal review.

Software without governance is just expensive noise.

Send this to whoever is defending the new software budget this quarter.
